what: Blind A/B over the shipped and candidate skill text. Six cold agents, each given a skill body, its correction reference, and a real doctor report covering all four finding families, asked to perform only the sorting step and to flag where they inferred rather than applied a stated rule. On the shipped text both runs sorted correctly but both reported that no sentence covers a repair naming no skill, and that the MCP family is not mentioned anywhere. On the candidate both reported no inference on the routing decision.

A sentence added during this mission — match a repair to its finding by the path it names, never by its position — was itself under-determined, and two independent blind runs hit the same tie: two findings at one path produce two repairs the path alone cannot separate. Re-derived from the report assembly, which maps findings in order through a map keyed on the whole repair pair, so help follows findings order and collapses only a word-for-word identical repair. Restated to that, with what each repair says to do as the tiebreak. The same class of defect this change request exists to fix, caught by the same method.

First cold spec-judge round returned blocked on a governance pre-flight failure: the dispatch declared an empty governance set. Correct — the inline spec-producer had run without one. Resolved the chain against the project registry (every bar resolves to the SDD default; the judge's claim of a plugin squad for this artifact-type does not hold against the matcher), loaded the three spec-gate actor bars and the two format bars, self-aligned, and re-dispatched a cold judge with the declared set.

Cold impl-judge failed one frozen scenario and was right. The handoff rule shipped as 'a repair naming the init skill goes to init, one naming no skill is work for a person', but six of the nine bridge repairs render a runnable init command line and name the skill nowhere, so an agent applying it literally routed a rebuildable bridge to a person - contradicting the scenario that hands exactly that finding to init. The explore evidence missed it because the fixture's only bridge fault was one of the three a rebuild would not fix. Rebuilt the fixture to carry a degraded bridge, reproduced the misroute on the pre-fix text in a blind run, and corrected the rule to ask whether the repair names init in either form. Verified mechanically over the whole table rather than by eye: the ten init-owned problems name it, the thirteen ownerless ones name neither, and the four this skill owns never reach the question. Pinned with a test so the two sets cannot drift apart again.
